title: Gateway bridging and structured output fallback acceptance
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Customer integrations that bridge Redwood streaming structured outputs into external tool gateways (third-party APIs, internal job queues, or webhook processors) observe two failure modes: (1) partial/fragmented JSON or typed frames that cause the gateway to reject the payload, and (2) transient downstream failures that require deferred or idempotent retries. This ticket defines the acceptance criteria for a gateway-bridging contract and fallback matrix that engineering will implement and Product will validate before release.

Goal: Provide deterministic rules and observable signals so SDKs, the runtime, and gateway adapters can: (A) anchor schemas early in a streaming session, (B) emit recoverable checkpoint frames that gateways can safely persist or resume from, and (C) classify failures to choose between immediate retries, deferred requeueing, or human operator handoff. The outcome should reduce integration errors and mean time to recovery for bridged tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: Schema anchoring: At stream start, the runtime must emit an initial 'schema-anchor' frame that contains a compact schema id and human-readable schema summary. Gateways that receive anchor + subsequent frames must be able to validate envelope ordering and detect missing anchors within 100ms of stream start.

Checkpoint frames: For long-running or chunked emits (>2s or >512 tokens), the runtime must periodically emit 'checkpoint' frames containing stable partial-object delimiters and a monotonic checkpoint id. Gateways must be able to persist a checkpoint and resume accepting frames starting at checkpoint+1.

Idempotent toolcalls: When an external tool is invoked via a gateway and the runtime detects a transient delivery or gateway error (5xx or connection reset), it must mark the call as retryable with a deterministic idempotency key and not duplicate side effects when retried within the configured window (default 60s).

Graceful degrade modes: Define and implement three degrade behaviors: failfast (return error to caller), buffered-defer (persist payload to dead-letter or queue for replay), and approximate-response (return best-effort structured object with 'partial=true' plus provenance). The chosen mode must be configurable per-route and per-customer and visible in the Console when active.

Observable classifications: Telemetry must differentiate error classes: parsing-failure (malformed frames), anchor-missing, checkpoint-mismatch, gateway-transient, gateway-permanent, and operator-required. Each produced error must include at least one of these labels in logs and traces.

Round-trip tests: End-to-end automated tests must validate a) a perfect path (schema-anchor + chunks + final commit), b) lost-chunk recovery using checkpoint resume, c) gateway transient error with idempotent retry preserves single side-effect, and d) fallback to buffered-defer with replay verifies final result after replay. All tests must be runnable in CI with a mocked gateway harness.

Backward compatibility: For customers not opting into new frame types, the runtime must continue producing legacy streamed JSON frames for 6 months after launch and document migration steps. No breaking changes allowed without a migration flag and 30-day notice.

SDK and gateway contract: SDKs (JS, Python) must provide helpers to parse anchors/checkpoints and expose recommended persistence semantics for gateways. Example helper APIs and code samples must be added to the docs site before release.

Operator playbook: Create an operator runbook for 'anchor-missing' and 'checkpoint-mismatch' incidents with clear steps for triage, manual resume, and customer communication templates. Playbook must be linked in Console incident actions (button to open runbook).
scope: In scope: new stream frame types (schema-anchor, checkpoint, partial-commit), telemetry labels for gateway errors, SDK parsing helpers, configurable per-route fallback policy, CI harness for gateway simulations, Console UX to surface active fallbacks and replay controls, operator runbook.
out_of_scope: Out of scope: changing underlying model generation semantics, new cryptographic anchors for schema verification (MVP uses signed checkpoints in next phase), on-prem installer changes for air-gapped networks.
success_metrics: Decrease in customer-reported integration failures to gateways by 70% within 30 days of rollout
Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) for gateway-related incidents from 2.5 hours to <30 minutes
Increase percentage of resumed streams that complete successfully after checkpoint resume to >= 95%
test_plan: Unit tests for framing encode/decode and checkpoint id monotonicity
Integration tests: mocked gateway harness replicating 200, 400, 500, connection reset during streams, with assertions for emitted telemetry and persisted checkpoints
Chaos test in staging: randomly drop chunk frames and verify resume path completes, run 1000 randomized sessions
Manual verification: product-led session with two pilot customers (internal staging + 'Acme Corp' pilot) to exercise SDK parsing helpers and console replay UI
Security test: threat model review for idempotency keys to ensure no sensitive data leakage and run static analysis on SDK helpers
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged canary (5% of users) in hosted runtime for 48 hours with tight telemetry alerting on parse-failure and anchor-missing rates
Expand to 25% for 72 hours if canary stable; run automated replay jobs to verify buffered-defer path
Open pilot for enterprise customers on Dedicated with opt-in config; run migration checklist
Default enable for all hosted customers after 30 days and communication via Console banner + changelog
Post-rollout retrospective: review alerts and customer tickets at 7 and 30 days
notes: Trade-offs: Signed cryptographic anchors provide stronger tamper-proofing but add key management complexity; deferred to follow-up. MVP uses schema-id + human summary (non-signed).
Decision: Use monotonic numeric checkpoint ids rather than byte offsets to simplify gateway persistence semantics across heterogeneous gateways.
Implementation constraint: Some low-latency routes cannot afford frequent checkpoints; default checkpoint rate will be configurable and suggestions provided by Optimize tooling later.
Related work: This intersects with Observability initiative for per-token tracing (ENG-39877) and Dedicated autoscaling recovery patterns (ENG-40910).
